key_idea: One hour is a sliding sort: position i receives the minimum of the k-1 elements carried along plus the newly entering element, so a pass is O(n log k) with a min-heap; simply simulate passes until sorted.
sketch: Keep a min-heap of the first k-1 elements; for each i from k-1 to n-1 push a[i], pop the minimum and write it to the next output slot; finally flush the heap in order. Repeat while the array is not sorted, counting passes (0 if already sorted). Each pass moves every element at most k-1 positions left and the small elements steadily settle, so there are at most about n/(k-1)+1 passes, giving O(n^2 log k / k), worst case k=2 with 2499 passes on 2500 elements (instant). Duplicates are harmless since only the value sequence matters. Stress-tested against the literal window-sorting simulation on 400 random small cases.
